'''Stefan Hecht''' (born 6 January 1974) is a German chemist.

== Life ==
{{BLP sources section|date=March 2021}}
Hecht was born in 1974 in East Berlin.<ref name="CV">[https://www.eurasc.org/storage/cv/853-1633338611.pdf Curriculum Vitae der ''European Academy of Sciences''] retrieved 1 January 2022.</ref> He studied chemistry from 1992 to 1997 at the [[Humboldt University of Berlin|Humboldt-Universität zu Berlin]] and the [[University of California, Berkeley]], where he carried out his diploma thesis research with the late William G. Dauben about "New Mechanistic Insight into the Lumiketone Rearrangement – Wavelength-Dependent [[Photochemistry]] of 4-Methoxybicyclo[3.1.0]hex-3-en-2-ones".<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Dauben|first1=William G.|last2=Hecht|first2=Stefan|date=1998|title=Wavelength-Dependent Photochemistry of 4-Methoxybicyclo[3.1.0]hexenones †|url=https://pubs.acs.org/doi/10.1021/jo970978n|journal=The Journal of Organic Chemistry|language=en|volume=63|issue=18|pages=6102–6107|doi=10.1021/jo970978n|pmid=11672235|issn=0022-3263|url-access=subscription}}</ref> After his diploma in chemistry, he carried out his graduate work from 1997 to 2001 on the "Synthesis and Application of Functional Branched Macromolecules – From Site Isolation and Energy Harvesting to Catalysis" in the research group of [[Jean Fréchet]] at the University of California, Berkeley.

After his return to Germany in the fall of 2001, Hecht established his independent research program as one of the first Sofja Kovalevskaja Awardees, initially as a Young Investigator at the [[Freie Universität Berlin]] and since 2005 as group leader at the [[Max Planck Institute for Coal Research]] in Mülheim upon Ruhr. In the fall of 2006 he became the youngest W3-professor in chemistry in Germany and holder of the chair of organic chemistry and functional materials at Humboldt-Universität zu Berlin. From 2019 until 2022 he was the scientific director of the DWI – Leibniz Institute for Interactive Materials in Aachen and held the chair for macromolecular chemistry at [[RWTH Aachen University]]. Since the fall of 2022 he is Einstein Professor<ref>{{Cite web |title=Stefan Hecht – Einstein Foundation Berlin |url=https://www.einsteinfoundation.de/en/fellows-projects/einstein-fellows-professors/einstein-professors/stefan-hecht/ |access-date=2023-02-18 |website=www.einsteinfoundation.de}}</ref> at Humboldt-Universität zu Berlin and founding director of the Center for the Science of Materials Berlin (CSMB).

Hecht is co-founder of the start-up company xolo GmbH that has been developing and commercializing xolography as new volumetric 3D printing technology since 2019.

He is married and father of two adult daughters.

== Research ==
Hecht is a synthetic chemist with research interests that span from macromolecular and [[supramolecular chemistry]] over photochemistry and [[electrochemistry]] all the way to surface and interface phenomena. Particular focus of his work is on the development of photoswitchable molecules to optically control of physical, chemical, and biological processes and their application in materials, (opto)electronic devices, and additive manufacturing.

Together with Martin Regehly he has invented xolography.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Regehly|first1=Martin|last2=Garmshausen|first2=Yves|last3=Reuter|first3=Marcus|last4=König|first4=Niklas F.|last5=Israel|first5=Eric|last6=Kelly|first6=Damien P.|last7=Chou|first7=Chun-Yu|last8=Koch|first8=Klaas|last9=Asfari|first9=Baraa|last10=Hecht|first10=Stefan|date=24 December 2020|title=Xolography for linear volumetric 3D printing|url=http://www.nature.com/articles/s41586-020-3029-7|journal=Nature|language=en|volume=588|issue=7839|pages=620–624|doi=10.1038/s41586-020-3029-7|pmid=33361791|bibcode=2020Natur.588..620R |s2cid=229689068 |issn=0028-0836|url-access=subscription}}</ref>  Xolography is a volumetric 3D printing method, which enables the rapid manufacturing of complex objects and entire systems directly in volume with high precision (resolution) and high material quality (homogeneous material with smooth surfaces). The technology and its application in additive manufacturing are being developed by the start-up company xolo GmbH, which he helped to co-found.

* 2020: member of the German Academy of Science and Engineering ([[acatech]])
* 2020: member of [[Academia Europaea]]
* 2012: starting grant (consolidator phase) of the [[European Research Council]] (ERC)
* 2010: [[Klung Wilhelmy Science Award|Klung-Wilhelmy-Weberbank-Prize]] in Chemistry
* 2005: ADUC Young Investigator Award by the [[German Chemical Society]]
* 2004: MIT's Technology Review [[TR35|TR100]] Top 100 Young Innovator Award
* 2001–2004: [[Sofia Kovalevskaya Award]] of the [[Alexander von Humboldt Foundation]]
* 1994–1997: fellow of the [[Studienstiftung]] des Deutschen Volkes
* 1993: [[Jugend forscht|Jugend Forscht]] Young Chemist Award (federal, regional & environmental prize)
* 1991: [[Jugend forscht|Jugend Forscht]] Young Chemist Award (regional prize)
